structure: Part 9, the live-animals snag list. Read in full: e2e/snagging.fit.spec.js (557 lines, 37 tests in 12 describes, S01 to S38 with S30 left out), e2e/support/snagging.js (63 lines: shoot, shootNoJs, shootMobile screenshot helpers), e2e/support/journey.js (283 lines: URL helpers, journey step helpers and the species and address fixtures) and e2e/support/fixtures.js (48 lines: the visited-pages recorder). Each snag test walks the live-animals journey to the page state a designer snag is about and takes full-page screenshots (desktop, and where named, with JavaScript off or at phone width). Most tests assert little beyond reaching the page; the claims record each page state reached, every selector, label, option, copy string and branch the tests assert or drive, and the snag number. Describes covered: origin of the import (S01-S05), what are you importing (S06-S08), main import reason (S09-S12), commodity details (S13-S14), identification details (S15-S18), arrival details (S19-S23), transit countries (S24-S25), transporter details (S26-S27), upload documents (S28, S29, S31), consignment addresses (S32, S33, S36, S37), review your notification (S34, S35) and notification submitted (S38). From the shared journey.js only the helpers this spec calls are claimed; the germinal helpers, the error-summary and back-link assertions and the reference reader are other parts' to claim.
